title: Validate artifact names against format, semantic and technical rules

facts.note: Task text mentions declaring, referencing, using or validating an artifact name or its contract.
Example locations only (contract schemas, plan/wagon produce/consume declarations); not exclusive scope gates — any file that declares or references an artifact name is in scope.

values: artifact name declared, referenced or used
consumer reference to an artifact added or changed
facts.note: Diff-level observer must extract artifact names and their references, plus contract $id/path changes, whether or not the name itself changed.
Name validator or review reporting a format, semantic or technical violation, including on existing names.

fires: A new artifact name is declared in a produce/consume list.
An existing artifact is renamed or gets a variant.
A consumer adopts an existing, unchanged artifact name whose contract file is missing.
A contract's $id or file path is edited so it no longer matches the artifact name, without renaming the artifact.
A contract schema whose $id carries an artifact name is authored or referenced.
A validator or review reports a violation on any existing artifact name.
doesNotFire: Edits to acceptance prose that neither declare, reference nor change any artifact name or its contract.
Changes to identifiers that are not artifact names (e.g. test function names, local variables).

given: A plan, wagon, acceptance, contract or consumer declares, references, uses or validates an artifact name
when: that name, a reference to it, or its contract file/$id is added, used or changed
then: The artifact name must pass all three validation rule categories — format, semantic and technical.
prefer: Format: theme lowercase with no separators; category/aspect/variant kebab-case; ':' for descent (hierarchy levels); '.' for variants.
Semantic: theme from the approved taxonomy; each hierarchy level adds value; aspect a concrete noun; variant a state/type/facet.
Technical: a contract file exists at contracts/{segments}.schema.json, where {segments} is derived by splitting the name on ':' and '.'; its $id is urn:contract:{artifact_name}.
The URN matches the name exactly, and all consumers reference that same name.
avoid: A URN that differs in any way from the name.
Consumers referencing a different spelling or alias of the name.
Hierarchy levels that add no value.
why: The name is the join key between plans, contracts and consumers; deriving format, meaning and file path from one name lets contracts be located mechanically and catches drift.
evidence: Each artifact name meets the format rule (lowercase theme without separators, kebab-case category/aspect/variant, ':' descent, '.' variants).
Theme is in the approved taxonomy; levels add value, aspect is a concrete noun, variant is a state/type/facet, no deep variant nesting; URN matches the name exactly.
contracts/{segments}.schema.json exists for the name, its $id equals urn:contract:{artifact_name}, and all consumer references use the identical name.
verifier_detail: validation_rule term: a format/semantic/technical constraint on artifact names; categories = [format, semantic, technical].

Format check: theme segment is lowercase and contains no separators; category/aspect/variant segments are kebab-case; ':' separates hierarchy levels (descent), '.' separates variants. The source does not further restrict the theme alphabet (e.g. digits) — do not add restrictions beyond lowercase/no separators.

Technical check: split the name on ':' and '.' to obtain {segments}; expect contracts/{segments}.schema.json to exist; expect its $id == 'urn:contract:' + artifact_name exactly; collect all consumer references and require identical names. The source does not specify how {segments} are joined into the path; use the repository's existing contract layout rather than inventing one. Apply to existing/unchanged names when they are newly referenced or their contract changes.

Semantic checks: theme membership is checked against the approved taxonomy (the taxonomy itself is maintained outside this rule); 'each level adds value', 'aspect is a concrete noun', 'variant is a state/type/facet' and 'no deep variant nesting' are llm_judged — the source gives no numeric nesting threshold. 'URN matches name exactly' is a deterministic string equality.

splitSuggestion.then: Artifact names must use a lowercase separator-free theme, kebab-case category/aspect/variant, ':' for descent and '.' for variants.
Artifact names must use an approved-taxonomy theme with value-adding levels, a concrete-noun aspect, a state/type/facet variant, a URN matching the name exactly, and no deep variant nesting.
Each artifact name must resolve to contracts/{segments}.schema.json (path derived by splitting on ':' and '.') whose $id is urn:contract:{artifact_name}, referenced identically by all consumers.
